question: Which city, and which neighborhood, should the move be to?
answer: Park Slope, unless the interview puts the role inside model decisions, which only San Francisco offers.
$comment: The content stage for this deck, written after the fact so the stage has a worked example that is a real deck rather than a fixture. Nothing here names a component, an architecture or a variant - `settles.kind` is the only field the layout stage reads. Compare `adds` against `claim` on every page: where the two say the same thing the page has no commentary column to earn.

pages.claim: Lead with Park Slope; move to SF only for a role inside model decisions

settles.what: the five gates scored across both cities and their shortlisted neighborhoods

pages.adds: Four gates resolve on evidence already gathered, so the interview is the only thing left that can reverse the answer
pages.highlight: clears every gate with evidence in hand

pages.claim: Both cities offer the role; only Anthropic lets you take it in New York

settles.what: published base-salary bands for the four product roles at both labs

pages.adds: The bands overlap enough that pay decides nothing; what separates the offers is which decisions the seat owns

pages.claim: NYC schools beat their peers by 7–12 points; the SF pair is a preference

settles.what: state proficiency against district and state peers for the four shortlisted schools

pages.adds: Education does not decide the city; it decides the neighborhood, and it has to be fixed before entry year rather than after the move

pages.claim: Hoboken is safest on the matched measure; neighborhoods differ more than cities

settles.what: violent crime per 1,000 residents across the six shortlisted neighborhoods

pages.adds: The within-city spread is wider than the between-city gap, so a city-level safety argument settles nothing either way
pages.highlight: get the rates before signing a lease

pages.claim: Every shortlisted commute fits in 45 minutes except Berkeley, which fails by 10

settles.what: door-to-door transit time by leg for each neighborhood against a 45-minute budget

pages.adds: Berkeley is the only option that fails on a measure with no remedy short of moving again, which is why it leaves the list rather than scoring low
pages.highlight: Ride time is not the constraint

pages.claim: Rent moves five points of gross pay: a comfort decision, not a viability one

settles.what: rent as a share of gross pay at each neighborhood's median two-bedroom

pages.adds: Five points is inside the range a stage-one rental can absorb, so rent should not be allowed to outrank the role

pages.claim: Hoboken is the midtown fallback: cheapest and safest, but its school trails its district

settles.what: the same five gates for Hoboken against Park Slope

pages.adds: It wins on the two gates that are cheapest to change later and loses on the one that is hardest, which is the wrong way round for a family move

pages.claim: Every gate resolves on evidence except the role, which only the interview can settle

settles.what: each gate, its evidence state, and what would still change it

pages.adds: Name the two questions to ask in the interview now, because after an offer the answer is no longer free to act on

pages.claim: Rent for stage one, book two visits, and fix the school before entry year

settles.what: the three actions, their timing and what each one depends on

pages.adds: Renting keeps the reversal cheap while the role question is still open, which is the only reason to delay buying
pages.highlight: the role with the closest researcher contact
